idiom_name: googletest/gMock mock class over the service interface (MOCK_METHOD)
implementation_notes: The dominant realization is a generated mock class: derive MockPriceService from the abstract PriceService and declare each operation with MOCK_METHOD, which synthesizes the override so the stand-in is checked against the interface at compile time, and EXPECT_CALL states the canned answers per test. The interface needs a virtual destructor, and production code should hold it by reference or smart pointer instead of by value. gRPC's C++ plugin supplies the production counterpart (the generated Stub class bound to a channel), while a hand-written fake stays justified when the test wants readable canned behaviour rather than interaction verification, and a free-function API with no interface at all can be substituted at link time with -Wl,--wrap.
pitfalls: The interface needs a virtual destructor: deleting a mock through a base pointer without one corrupts state, and the gMock documentation calls this out as the first rule.
When a mock is heap-allocated its lifetime must end before the test ends, otherwise the destructor never runs and gMock never verifies the expectations.

Expectations must be set before the mock is called: alternating EXPECT_CALL with calls is documented as undefined behaviour, and a dangling reference in a lambda-based expectation is a use-after-free.

variants.name: Hand-written final fake implementing the abstract interface
variants.implementation_notes: A small final class with canned members - or a std::function per operation - keeps the whole stand-in inside the test file and reads as data rather than as expectations. Choose it when the test only needs answers, and keep gMock for interaction checking; hold either behind std::unique_ptr<PriceService> so no concrete type leaks into the client.
pitfalls: Returning default-constructed values for unknown inputs hides client bugs: fail fast on inputs the fixture does not cover.
Storing the fake by value in the client slices it to the base class and silently calls the real behaviour instead of the stand-in.

variants.name: Generated gRPC client stub (production seam)
variants.idiom_name: Greeter::Stub from the protoc gRPC plugin
variants.implementation_notes: For the production seam the stand-in is generated rather than written: protoc plus the gRPC plugin emit a Stub class whose methods mirror the service and wrap parameters into protobuf messages before sending them over a channel. The client can then be compiled against a contract that has no server yet, and only the channel target changes between environments; the price is a codegen step and a version-locked IDL.
pitfalls: The generated stub is a client, not a test double: it still needs a reachable server, so tests either talk to a sandbox or to an in-process service implementation.
Regeneration must be part of the build; a stale generated stub compiles happily against an older contract.
